kill_argument: The figure a reader will look at for the wage contradicts the paper's own wage test. fig_event panel (b) draws California's post-window wage gaps with 95% bands built from the H2 (employment) statistic's critical values, c_hi(0.975) = 2.14 (runs/event-path/metrics.json). The pre-specified wage test H1 uses the wage statistic's own critical values, which the decision set L pushes to c_hi(0.95) = 3.45 and c_hi(0.975) = 4.32 (runs/h1-wage/metrics.json, Lq_h1_* in runs/level-mde), and on that basis H1 is 'not supported'. With the H2 values, 6 of the 8 post quarters have a wage band entirely above zero; with H1's c_hi(0.975), none do (my arithmetic on runs/event-path/event_path.csv). The generated caption says only that 'both panels use these critical values, as the run does' and that the bands 'are not those intervals'; it never says that the wage test's upper critical value is twice as large, so a referee reads panel (b) as a significant wage effect in nearly every quarter next to a text that says H1 fails. What I attacked and what held: I ran fig_event, fig_placebo and fig_select on the real run outputs, writing only to my scratch folder (no estimate, only redraws); all exit 0 and every internal consistency check passes; the C3 SDID-floor caption logic matches sclib.critical_values and refuses tampered inputs; crew.py validate passes and no recorded run uses a changed file.

findings.text: fig_event panel (b) (wage) uses the H2 statistic's critical values (c_hi(0.975) = 2.14, c_lo(0.025) = -2.14 at nu = 14.06), as analysis_plan 16 says. For the selected DDT-POPW-E-R50 the wage statistic's own critical values are far larger on the upper side: Lq_h1_q95 = 3.45 and Lq_h1_q975 = 4.32 set h1_c_hi95 and h1_c_hi975, and H1 is 'not supported' because t = 2.66 < 3.45. On the real event_path.csv, the panel (b) band excludes zero in 6 of 8 post quarters (2024Q2, 2024Q3, 2025Q2, 2025Q3, 2025Q4, 2026Q1) with H2's c_hi(0.975), and in none with H1's c_hi(0.975). The caption the script generates (and that the Writer must use unchanged) states the H2 values and says the bands are not the pooled intervals, but does not state H1's critical values or that the wage band would be about twice as wide on the upper side under them. The figure therefore shows a pattern the paper's pre-specified wage test rejects. The design text fixed the H2 critical values for both panels before the L quantile for the wage was known; the problem is in what the caption leaves out, not in a wrong number.
findings.evidence: code/fig_event.py lines 47-48, 68-70 and caption lines 196-201, 210-214; runs/event-path/metrics.json c_hi975 2.1439; runs/h1-wage/metrics.json h1_c_hi95 3.4487, h1_c_hi975 4.3204, h1_t 2.663, h1_reject 0; runs/level-mde/metrics.json Lq_h1_q95/q975; runs/event-path/event_path.csv wage rows with post = 1; plan.json design.analysis_plan 16. Remedy (cheapest, no deviation): fig_event.py reads runs/h1-wage/metrics.json (declared as an --input) and the caption states, for panel (b), H1's one-sided critical values c_hi(0.95) and c_hi(0.975) next to the H2 ones, says the wage band uses the smaller H2 values and so is narrower on the upper side than the H1 test, and says how many post quarters' bands exclude zero under each (or simply that a band excluding zero in panel (b) is not evidence against H1's label). Alternative: draw panel (b) with H1's critical values (arithmetic from gap and se in event_path.csv), recorded as a deviation from analysis_plan 16 before fig-event runs.
